messages.author: 7a1a0c66d60b0f26
messages.subject: MQM analysis
parts:
Hi all,
I have been using R/qtl and MQM analysis to examine a number of
phenotypes in an F2 cross. Due to the computing time required for
calculating penalties for stepwiseqtl() I haven't used this function
much yet but I am planning to. I have also now been working with the
cofactor selection and mqmscan() calls in the newest tutorial. My
question is this: aside from the penalized LOD thresholds used in the
stepwiseqtl() algorithm what, if any, are the major differences
between these methods (especially calling makeqtl() and fitqtl() vs.
mqmsetcofactors() and mqmscan() )? I understand that cofactor
selections are automated with the latter method but is this any
different than running fitqtl() and then addqtl() and addint() and
"doing it by hand"?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] MQM analysis
parts:
There are differences in how the models are fit. (That is, how the missing genotype data at putative QTL is accommodated.). The other major difference concerns the evaluation of the quality of a model (or its terms). MQM makes use of the estimated residual SD under a "full model" with all marker covariates, while fitqtl and related functions estimate the residual SD separately for each QTL model.

karl

messages.subject: Re: MQM analysis
parts:
Thank you for your reply Karl. If you don't mind I have another
question, this time focusing on the stepwiseqtl() function.

I have my penalties in hand and have used them to analyze a phenotype
which i previously modeled using fitqtl() etc. With stepwiseqtl() the
best model is one including a major locus and 6 minor loci, 5 of which
are on the same linkage group. If I use this model in the fitqtl()
function I find support for including them in terms of LOD scores,
however, the pve is very low. More importantly, if I try to build this
model using fitqtl(), addqtl(), and addint() I don't get any farther
than the major locus in a single qtl model.

Can you shed some light on why this may be and how you would interpret
these results?

Thank you very much in advance.

Nick

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: MQM analysis
parts:
You can get artifacts in the fit of tightly linked QTL, especially if there are phenotype outliers. This may be going on with your data. Ideally, you want at least two markers between any two QTL, but I think even then you can get artifacts.

Also, the calculation of percent variance explained in fitqtl seems to not be appropriate for linked QTL.

karl
